dedupe_keys.name: equer life cycle assessment of buildings and districts mines paris

description: EQUER is a tool for assessing the environmental quality of buildings by life cycle assessment, developed since 1995 at the École des Mines de Paris together with the software publisher IZUBA Energies. It was extended to districts, combining several building types, public spaces such as roads and green areas, and networks such as water and district heating, to support eco-district design. The page explains that life cycle assessment follows a product from resource extraction through use to end of life, and that EQUER adapts this to buildings and districts, which are usually unique projects tied to their site and occupants; users include urban planners, architects, engineering offices and manufacturers. Coverage: French construction practice. Access: through Mines Paris and IZUBA Energies. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: the documentation is in French, and results depend on the life cycle inventory data used. Simulation uses: comparing environmental impacts of building and district design options, including public space and networks. Related records: the OKOBAUDAT construction LCA database and the CLF whole-building LCA benchmark.
